text:
Priya: Quick sync — we need a clean decision for Private/VPC handoff when customers can't accept peering (cost or policy). Is the minimal-trust split with an ephemeral private endpoint + relay still our fav? 
Miguel: I think so, but the wire details matter. ephemeral endpoints + encrypted tunnel to regional relays seems lowest ops for customers.
Sam: What about IP preservation? Some customers require source-IP for downstream ACLs. A relay will NAT.
Lindsey: If IP preservation is mandatory we either need per-customer ENI (expensive) or TCP proxy with original IP via proxy-protocol + customer-side proxy. Both are heavy.
Priya: Right — two buckets: (1) customers who tolerate NAT/fallback paths, (2) customers needing source IP. For (1) ephemeral endpoints + relay. For (2) recommend dedicated ENI/dedicated peering.
Miguel: Also TLS termination: do we terminate on the regional relay or pass-through to customer controlplane? Terminating lets us do connection multiplexing and mTLS to backend but increases trust surface.
Sam: If we terminate we must support cert pinning + strict audit. For private deployments maybe customer-managed certs in KMS a must.
Lindsey: Option: SNI passthrough to customer controlplane with a lightweight TCP forwarder (no TLS terminate). That preserves E2E auth but prevents us from doing token-level traces at relay.
Priya: Tradeoffs clear. My leaning: default path = SNI passthrough over an ephemeral private endpoint to regional relay that forwards to customer endpoint (no TLS termination). Opt-in path = relay TLS terminate for observability with customer consent + rotate certs.
Miguel: Agreed. We should standardize the handshake: ephemeral endpoint gets a short-lived cert from our CA, customer accepts CA during onboarding. Relay establishes a mTLS session to controlplane inside customer VPC.
Sam: Can we outline the handshake in a tiny example?
Lindsey: Sure, rough flow:
```
# customer creates private endpoint (VPC endpoint or peered ENI)
# ephem-agent registers IP to control plane: POST /register {cidr, az, ttl}
# control plane issues short cert (TTL=1h) signed by redwood-ephem-ca
# agent uses cert to open TLS to regional-relay: 10.x.y.z:443 -> relay validates cert
```
Sam: Also need a renew path and an offline revocation list for emergency churn. CRLs are slow; we should support immediates via controlplane push + LRU drop on relay.
Priya: Security question: if relay is compromised can it MITM customer traffic when we do termination? We need a policy: only terminate when tenant has given explicit write consent and has an ACL that permits termination.
Miguel: Add telemetry: any termination event must be logged to customer audit logs and trigger a webhook.
Lindsey: Ops concern: scaling ephemeral endpoints — we could multiplex many customer agents over a small pool of connections using ALPN-based tenant routing, but that breaks IP preservation and complicates troubleshooting.
Priya: For capacity planning let's assume churn 2k ephemeral endpoints/hour for mid-sized rollout. Relay autoscaling must be reactive to concurrent streams not endpoints.
Sam: Implementation note: in k8s relay we can use `haproxy` with `tcp-request content` rules and `alpn` mapping. Example config snippet: 
```
frontend fe_ephem
  bind *:443
  mode tcp
  tcp-request inspect-delay 5s
  tcp-request content accept if { req_ssl_hello_type 1 }
  use_backend bk_tenant_%[req_ssl_sni]
```
Lindsey: That ALPN/SNI mapping works but SNI string length and sanitization matter. We need canonical tenant ids in SNI (no spaces, base32).
Miguel: Operationalization: rolling cert rotation + 0-downtime handshake: ensure agent keeps old cert until new session is validated. Also provide a debug command for customers: `redwood-agent diag tunnel-status` that dumps active session fingerprint.
Priya: Action items: 
- Miguel: draft the handshake diagram + sequence (proto + cert lifecycle) — due EOD Thu.
- Sam: validate SNI mapping limitations for AWS/GCP/private endpoints and propose fallback (ALPN token) — due Tue.
- Lindsey: add ops runbook for relay compromise scenarios + audit webhook spec — due Mon.
Sam: One more thing — billing & cost: ephemeral endpoints that bypass peering will have egress hops on our side. We should have a chargeback estimate + throttle suggestions in console.
Priya: Good call, include a cost-per-GB estimate with regional delta.
